clue.text: Convey via throw in this direction?

parts.note: to put is to throw, as in putting the shot
the clue sits in the across list, so its own direction is across

explanation.surface: A question of how to pass something on by throwing it one way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in this direction?' points at the grid itself: this is an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something across is an idiom for communicating it successfully.

clue.text: Change over, touring unknown county

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the reversed word encloses the unknown
over signals that the word for change is turned round in this down entry

parts.note: to swop is to change or exchange
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone changes over while touring an unfamiliar part of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SWOP into POWS, and 'touring' puts Y inside it. POWYS is a county in mid Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Powys is a Welsh administrative county, so it is an example of a county.

clue.text: New light shed now on dead men?

definitions.text: New light shed now on dead men?

parts.words: New light shed now on dead men?
parts.note: dead men are emptied bottles, and the new light is the dawn that shows them after a night of drinking

explanation.surface: A fresh discovery throws light on the deceased.
explanation.walkthrough: In pub slang a 'dead man' is an empty bottle; the dawn after a binge reveals them, and the phrase also means a hangover.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the following day's dawn and, by extension, the hangover that greets a heavy drinker.

clue.text: "Church admits more than half drink:" one's exclusive

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the church abbreviation holds the other pieces
only the first four of the six letters of the drink are kept, which is more than half

parts.note: liquor is alcoholic drink
one is I, and the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A church lets in a drinker, and someone remarks on their exclusivity.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon and quotation marks make the clue look like a quoted remark; 'more than half' means four of the drink's six letters survive.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cliquish means forming a closed group that shuts others out, a sense of exclusive.

clue.text: Place order, stock being empty

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its insides, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Instructions to order goods while the stockroom is bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Omsk is a Siberian city, so it is an example of a place.

clue.text: Is she next to crack under son's intuition?

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means placed below, so the scrambled words follow the son

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: cracking breaks something up, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether a woman will be next to break under her son's insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to crack' scrambles IS SHE NEXT into IXTHSENSE, which sits 'under' S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixth sense is a supposed extra faculty of perception beyond the five, that is, intuition.

clue.text: Lead pumped out by people killing chickens

indicators.note: the leading letter is expelled from the word for killers

parts.note: slayers are people who kill

explanation.surface: Bullets fired by killers end up hitting poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead pumped out' removes the first letter S of SLAYERS; the surface suggests gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: Layers are hens kept for laying eggs, so they are chickens.

clue.text: Ford mentions links in writing

parts.note: to ford a river is to cross it
references are mentions

explanation.surface: A car maker, Ford, gets name-checked in print.
explanation.walkthrough: Ford looks like the car firm but is the verb meaning to wade across.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-references are notes in a text directing the reader to another passage, which are links in writing.

clue.text: Ruth's duty to express surprise thus

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity or compassion
an onus is a duty or burden

explanation.surface: The biblical Ruth has an obligation to show astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth looks like a name; here it is the old noun for pity, as in ruthless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old exclamation of astonishment, a way of expressing surprise.

clue.text: The air of becoming a square?

definitions.text: The air of becoming a square?

parts.words: The air of becoming a square?
parts.note: an air is a song, and the number sixty-four is the square of eight, so the song is about reaching that age

explanation.surface: Asking how one sounds when turning boring and old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: It is a Beatles song about growing old; 64 is 8 squared, and 'square' also means stuffy.
explanation.definitionFit: This Beatles song imagines reaching sixty-four, the square of eight, so it is the air of becoming a square.

clue.text: Governor's arm cut in the middle

indicators.note: the central letter of the seven-letter weapon is cut away

parts.note: a shotgun is a firearm

explanation.surface: A governor's arm is injured halfway along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut in the middle' drops T, the fourth of SHOTGUN's seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was the hereditary military ruler of Japan, effectively its governor.

clue.text: These cry out for location in Surrey

indicators.note: out suggests being disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Locals cry out for a place in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles THESE CRY. CHERTSEY is a town in Surrey, a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chertsey is a Thames-side town in the English county of Surrey.

clue.text: Nasty girl — one agitating in complaint

indicators.note: agitating means stirring up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nasty girl stirs up trouble in a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitating' rearranges NASTY GIRL plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngitis is an inflammation of the voice box, a medical complaint.

clue.text: It's a mistake to bury second fish in a heap

indicators.note: to bury is to put inside, so the blunder encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a boner is a blunder
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Burying a fish in a heap turns out to be an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' reads as a link here; a heap is slang for a battered old vehicle, and the bicycle sense is the original one.
explanation.definitionFit: A boneshaker is a rickety old vehicle, and a heap is slang for a decrepit car.

clue.text: Redraw as a screw in this?

definitions.text: Redraw as a screw in this?

parts.words: Redraw as a screw in this?
parts.note: written backwards, redraw spells a word for a prison officer, which is what screw means in prison slang

explanation.surface: Asking whether to redraw something as a fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw is British prison slang for a warder, and a slang that reads words backwards turns redraw into warder.
explanation.definitionFit: Back slang is a form of slang in which words are said backwards, so redraw would stand for a prison warder.

clue.text: Girl in short trousers

indicators.note: short means cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: jeans are denim trousers

explanation.surface: A girl wearing shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like it describes the trousers but cuts the last letter of JEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Before second half of nativity play opening scenes using animation

indicators.note: before says the play's opening part comes first in the answer

parts.note: the opening section of a play is Act I

indicators.note: the last four of the eight letters are taken

explanation.surface: Animation is used for the start of a nativity play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second half of' takes VITY from NATIVITY, and 'Before' puts ACT I first.
explanation.definitionFit: Activity means bustle and liveliness, which is a sense of animation.

clue.text: Hooter: getting out, stop working

definitions.meaning: hooter is slang for the nose
with 'getting out' added, the word gives a phrase meaning to break down

explanation.surface: Someone's nose gives out and stops functioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting out' tells you to add out: conk out means to break down. Hooter and conk are both British slang for the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Conk is slang for a nose, and to conk out is to stop working.

clue.text: Hollows ahead, made for lookouts?

parts.note: read ahead as a head: hollows in a head made to hold the organs that look out

explanation.surface: Dips in the road in front, built for sentries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' splits into 'a head', and the lookouts are the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The orbits of the skull are the hollows in a head that hold the eyes.

clue.text: Insecticide — greenfly swallowing an amount

indicators.note: the two words swallow, or contain, the answer within them

explanation.surface: Greenfly eat an amount of insecticide.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across insecticiDE GREEnfly.
explanation.definitionFit: A degree is an extent or amount, as in 'to some degree'.

clue.text: One in feud perhaps runs off after special constable in search

indicators.note: after places the remaining letters behind the constable abbreviation

parts.note: SC is a special constable, a volunteer British police officer

indicators.note: off means removed, so the cricket abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: an avenger is someone pursuing revenge, as in a feud
R stands for runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A feuding person flees after a police volunteer who is searching.
explanation.walkthrough: A special constable is a part-time volunteer officer in British policing; 'runs' is the cricket scoring abbreviation, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To scavenge is to search through waste for anything usable.

clue.text: Wife's new-size bust shrinks

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wife's new bust measurement turns out smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes bust a body part and new-size one adjective; split them and bust becomes the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To wizen is to shrivel or wither, which is to shrink.

clue.text: Demanding back

definitions.meaning: harsh and exacting, as a strict teacher is
the rear part of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Stern means strict and severe, and it is also the rear end of a boat.

clue.text: Typical playwright's not British

indicators.note: not says the British abbreviation is left out of the playwright

parts.note: Bertolt Brecht was a German playwright

explanation.surface: A typical dramatist who isn't from Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes BR from BRECHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German loanword meaning authentic or typical of its kind.

clue.text: You must be under this to see The Longest Day

definitions.text: You must be under this to see The Longest Day

parts.words: You must be under this to see The Longest Day
parts.note: The Longest Day sounds like the war film, but beyond this line of latitude the sun never sets in midsummer, giving a day lasting a full 24 hours

explanation.surface: A cinema age limit for watching a famous war film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' reads like an age limit; on a map it means south of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: South of this line of latitude the sun stays up for a whole day at midsummer, the longest day possible.

clue.text: Turn and run, say, retreating for stuff

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in 'your go'
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: eg means for example, which say also means

explanation.surface: Someone turns and runs, retreating with their stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff oneself with food.

clue.text: Adjust time, ultimately by curious round clock

parts.note: to set a clock is to adjust it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word
round means turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nosey means curious, prying

explanation.surface: Someone adjusts the time on a curious round clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Clock looks like the noun from the surface, but it is slang for to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock is slang for to notice or see, as is to set eyes on.
